description: Connecting the physical world to the Internet: sensing and actuation, IoT communication protocols, sensor networks and machine-to-machine systems, interoperability, Arduino and Raspberry Pi programming, software-defined networking, data handling and cloud, fog and sensor-cloud computing, and the application domains from smart cities to agriculture and health. Taught to the depth of a leading Internet of Things course.
modelledOn: Bahga and Madisetti, Internet of Things: A Hands-On Approach
Buyya and Dastjerdi, Internet of Things: Principles and Paradigms
Hanes, Salgueiro, Grossetete, Barton and Henry, IoT Fundamentals: Networking Technologies, Protocols, and Use Cases
Raj and Raman, The Internet of Things: Enabling Technologies, Platforms, and Use Cases
outcomes: Describe the IoT architecture from sensing and actuation through networking to applications.
Select and use IoT protocols such as MQTT, CoAP, HTTP, Zigbee, BLE, LoRaWAN and cellular IoT.
Design wireless sensor networks and machine-to-machine systems and address interoperability.
Program Arduino and Raspberry Pi devices with sensors and actuators and connect them to a cloud service.
Explain software-defined networking, fog and sensor-cloud computing in IoT deployments.
Build and evaluate an end-to-end IoT application in a domain such as agriculture, health or smart cities, with attention to security and privacy.

units.title: IoT, sensing, actuation and networking basics
topics: Definition and history of the IoT; things, gateways, platforms, applications; reference architectures (ITU-T, IoT-A)
Sensors (temperature, humidity, light, motion, gas, GPS) and actuators (relays, motors, valves); signal conditioning and ADC
Networking basics for IoT: IP, addressing, IPv6 and 6LoWPAN, constrained devices and networks
Characteristics: scale, heterogeneity, constrained resources, intermittent connectivity, data volume
Lab kit: Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, sensors; simulators (Wokwi, Tinkercad)

units.title: Communication protocols
topics: Physical and link layers: IEEE 802.15.4, Zigbee, Thread, Bluetooth Low Energy, Wi-Fi, LoRa/LoRaWAN, Sigfox, NB-IoT and LTE-M, RFID and NFC
Network and transport: 6LoWPAN, RPL, UDP versus TCP for IoT
Application protocols: MQTT (publish-subscribe, QoS, retained messages), CoAP, HTTP/REST, AMQP, WebSockets
Choosing a protocol for range, power, data rate and cost; running an MQTT broker and clients
Security in protocols: DTLS, TLS, device authentication

units.title: Sensor networks and machine-to-machine
topics: Wireless sensor networks: topologies, routing, clustering, energy-aware design, localisation and time synchronisation
Machine-to-machine communication; oneM2M and ETSI M2M architecture
Edge devices, gateways and protocol translation
Reliability and fault tolerance in sensor networks

units.title: Interoperability
topics: Levels of interoperability: device, network, syntactic, semantic, platform
Standards and data models: IPSO, OMA LwM2M, W3C Web of Things, Matter
Data formats: JSON, CBOR, SenML; ontologies (SSN/SOSA)
Integrating devices from different vendors through a gateway

units.title: Arduino programming with sensors and actuators
topics: Arduino and ESP32 programming model: setup and loop, digital and analog I/O, PWM, interrupts, timers
Reading sensors over analog, I2C and SPI; driving actuators and displays
Wi-Fi connectivity and sending telemetry over MQTT and HTTP; over-the-air updates
Power management and battery and solar operation
Mini-project: a soil-moisture monitor that publishes readings

units.title: Python and Raspberry Pi
topics: Raspberry Pi setup, Linux basics, GPIO with Python (gpiozero, RPi.GPIO), camera and USB devices
Raspberry Pi as a gateway: MQTT broker, local database, dashboard (Node-RED, Grafana)
Edge processing: filtering, aggregation, simple machine learning on the Pi
Remote access and device management

units.title: SDN for IoT
topics: Software-defined networking: control and data plane separation, OpenFlow, controllers
SDN benefits for IoT: traffic management, security policies, mobility, scalability
Network function virtualisation; SDN in wireless sensor networks and 5G
Simulating an SDN-managed IoT network with Mininet

units.title: Data handling, analytics and cloud
topics: IoT data characteristics; ingestion, time-series databases, storage and retention
Cloud IoT platforms: AWS IoT Core, Azure IoT Hub, Google Cloud IoT, ThingsBoard, open-source alternatives
Device registration, provisioning, digital twins, rules engines, alerts
Analytics and visualisation: dashboards, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance; machine learning at the edge

units.title: Sensor-cloud and fog computing
topics: Sensor-cloud architecture: virtual sensors, sensors as a service
Fog and edge computing: motivation (latency, bandwidth, privacy), architecture, placement of computation
Offloading and orchestration between device, fog and cloud
Designing a fog layer for a campus or farm deployment with intermittent Internet

units.title: Applications and case studies
topics: Smart cities (traffic, lighting, waste), smart homes, connected vehicles, smart grid and prepaid metering, industrial IoT and Industry 4.0
Case studies: precision agriculture and irrigation in Ghana, healthcare and remote patient monitoring, activity and fall monitoring
Security, privacy and safety of IoT systems: botnets (Mirai), device hardening, data protection
Capstone: an end-to-end IoT system from sensor to cloud dashboard, with a cost and power budget

schedule.title: IoT architecture, sensors and addressing
schedule.exercise: Draw a layered IoT reference architecture for a smart water meter and list the sensor, signal conditioning and network technology at each layer.

tasks.title: Connect a temperature sensor and a relay to a microcontroller on the bench and show the ADC reading switching the relay at 30 degrees
Assign IPv6 addresses to six constrained nodes and a border router in the network simulator and verify that packets reach every node
Draw an architecture diagram for a smart streetlight system mapping things, gateway, platform and application to a reference model and noting the data flows

schedule.title: Characteristics and lab kit
schedule.exercise: Short comparison: choose between Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi for three IoT scenarios and justify each choice.

tasks.title: Blink an LED and read a button on a simulated ESP32 board and note which pins and peripherals the board offers
Simulate 50 sensors sharing a link with intermittent connectivity and record how many readings are lost and the data volume per hour
Pick a board and sensors for a battery-powered cold-room monitor, wire the circuit in the simulator and check its current budget

schedule.title: IoT communication technologies
schedule.exercise: Compare four wireless technologies in a table of range, data rate, power and cost, and explain MQTT QoS levels in your own words.

tasks.title: Publish a temperature reading to an MQTT topic from a simulated sensor and subscribe to it from a second client, checking the payload
Select the radio technology for a farm sensor network from LoRaWAN, Zigbee, BLE and NB-IoT given range, battery and cost evidence, scored on a rubric
Compare UDP and TCP for a 10-second sensor reporting interval on a lossy wireless link in the simulator and report packet loss and overhead

schedule.title: Choosing protocols and securing them
schedule.exercise: Short design: pick a protocol stack for a soil sensor and write down how devices will authenticate to the broker.

tasks.title: Run an MQTT broker with three clients, set a retained message and test last will, observing each client's view of the topics
Choose between MQTT and CoAP for a battery-powered sensor by measuring bytes sent and radio on-time for each over 100 readings
Add TLS and client certificates to an IoT link in the simulator and show a device with a wrong certificate is rejected

schedule.title: Sensor networks and M2M
schedule.exercise: Draw a clustered sensor network on paper, choose cluster heads and estimate the energy saved over direct transmission.

tasks.title: Build a four-hop sensor network topology in the simulator and trace one reading from the farthest node to the sink
Configure a gateway that translates between a local sensor protocol and MQTT to the cloud, and verify values arrive in the right topics
Fail a relay node in a sensor network, observe the effect on delivery and add redundant paths so delivery stays above 95 percent

schedule.title: Interoperability
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page note on how you would integrate a thermometer from vendor A and a humidity sensor from vendor B into one dashboard.

tasks.title: Encode a temperature reading as JSON, CBOR and SenML and compare the byte sizes of each representation
Register a device with a LwM2M-style object model and read its resources from a client, checking the units and data types
Integrate two sensors using different payload formats through a gateway that normalises them to one schema, and test with malformed input

schedule.title: Arduino and ESP32 programming
schedule.exercise: Program a threshold alarm: read a sensor, compare to a limit, drive a buzzer and publish the state, and write a brief test plan.

tasks.title: Read a potentiometer and dim an LED with PWM using setup and loop, and add a timer interrupt that blinks a second LED
Read an I2C temperature sensor and an analog soil sensor, show both on an LCD and drive a relay when the soil is too dry
Send soil moisture readings to an MQTT broker over Wi-Fi, reconnect after a network drop and handle an over-the-air update message

schedule.title: Power and the soil moisture project
schedule.exercise: Mini-project report: a soil-moisture monitor with a circuit diagram, code description, power budget and test results.

tasks.title: Measure the current of a sensor node in sleep and active states and calculate battery life for a 2000 mAh cell
Size a solar panel and battery so that a field sensor reporting every 15 minutes survives five cloudy days in the simulator
Build a soil-moisture monitor that samples hourly, publishes to MQTT and sleeps between readings, and meet a one-month battery target

schedule.title: Raspberry Pi and edge processing
schedule.exercise: Document a Raspberry Pi gateway design with broker, database and dashboard, and list how you will manage it remotely.

tasks.title: Control an LED and read a button on Raspberry Pi GPIO with Python and log each press with a timestamp
Run an MQTT broker and a local database on a Raspberry Pi gateway and show a dashboard with the last 100 readings
Filter and aggregate noisy sensor data at the edge and train a small classifier that flags abnormal readings, reporting precision and recall

schedule.title: SDN for IoT
schedule.exercise: Short essay: explain how an SDN controller could prioritise alarm traffic over routine telemetry in a smart building.

tasks.title: Install flow rules on a simulated OpenFlow switch to forward sensor traffic to a gateway and watch the flow table counters change
Write flow rules that give alarm packets priority over telemetry and block an unknown device, then verify with test traffic
Build an SDN-managed IoT network with 20 sensors, reroute traffic around a failed link and measure the recovery time

schedule.title: IoT data, cloud and analytics
schedule.exercise: Design a data pipeline and retention plan for 1,000 sensors reporting every minute, and estimate the storage per year.

tasks.title: Create a storage bucket and load a day of sensor readings as time-stamped files, then list and read back the readings
Provision three devices on a managed IoT service, add a rule that triggers an alert at a threshold and check the notification
Detect anomalies in a stream of temperature data with a rolling z-score and use them to predict a failing pump within the margin of error

schedule.title: Fog computing for an intermittent farm
schedule.exercise: Design a fog layer for a farm with intermittent Internet, specifying what runs on devices, the fog node and the cloud.

tasks.title: Expose two physical sensors as virtual sensors through a cloud service and read both through a single API call
Compare round-trip latency and Internet bandwidth when sensor data is processed on a local fog node and when sent to the cloud
Design and test a farm deployment where a fog node buffers data during a six-hour outage and syncs it without loss when the link returns

schedule.title: Applications, security and the capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: system architecture, power and cost budget, security analysis and test results for an end-to-end IoT system.

tasks.title: Build a soil-moisture irrigation controller that switches a valve from sensor readings and logs each event, and verify it with simulated dry and wet soil
Defend an IoT network against a simulated Mirai-style scan by changing default credentials, disabling unused services and adding an ACL, then retest
Build an end-to-end IoT system from sensor to cloud dashboard and keep monthly cost and power within a stated budget under a 30-day simulation
